subject: Indian Constitution
s: Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution on the recommendations of
x: The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended Fundamental Duties, which the 42nd Amendment added as Article 51A.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: The term "Secular" was added to the Preamble of the Indian Constitution by
x: The 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 inserted the words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' into the Preamble.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Match List - I with List - II. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I (Borrowed Feature) / List - II (Source)
a. Emergency Provisions - i. United Kingdom
b. Suspension of Fundamental Rights during Emergency - ii. Australia
c. Concept of Concurrent List - iii. Government of India Act, 1935
d. Single Citizenship - iv. German Constitution
v. USA
x: Emergency provisions come from the Government of India Act 1935, suspension of rights during emergency from the Weimar (German) Constitution, the Concurrent List from Australia and single citizenship from the UK.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Which of the following statements are true regarding 97th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2011 ?
A. Gave Constitutional status and protection to Co-operative Societies.
B. Made the right to form Co-operative Societies a Fundamental Right under Article 19.
C. It added a new Part X-B to the Constitution.
D. Added new Directive Principle under Article 43-B.
Choose the right answer from the codes given below :
x: The 97th Amendment gave co-operatives constitutional status, added the right to form them to Article 19(1)(c) and inserted Article 43B, but the new part it added was Part IXB, not X-B.

s: constitution

subject: Indian Constitution
s: Which Article of the Indian Constitution is described as the "heart and soul" of the Constitution by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar ?
x: Ambedkar called Article 32, the right to constitutional remedies, the very soul and heart of the Constitution.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: Indian Constitution was adopted by the Constituent Assembly of India on
x: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949; it came fully into force on 26 January 1950.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: Which part of the Indian Constitution deals with the Union Executive ?
x: Part V (Articles 52-151) deals with the Union, including the President, Vice-President and Council of Ministers.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: How many Schedules were there in the original Indian Constitution ?
x: The Constitution as adopted in 1949 had eight Schedules; four more were added later, making twelve.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: When was the Human Rights Commission of India constituted ?
x: The National Human Rights Commission was set up on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Ordinance, later the 1993 Act.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Match List - I with List - II. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I (National Commission) / List - II (Name of First Chairperson)
a. National Commission for STs - i. Justice R. N. Prasad
b. National Commission for Minorities - ii. Kunwar Singh
c. National Commission for SCs - iii. Justice Mohammad Sardar Ali Khan
d. National Commission for BCs - iv. Suraj Bhan
x: The first chairpersons were Kunwar Singh Tekam (STs, 2004), Justice Mohammad Sardar Ali Khan (Minorities, 1993), Suraj Bhan (SCs, 2004) and Justice R. N. Prasad (BCs, 1993).

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct ?
A. Residuary powers of legislation are included in Article 248 of the Constitution of India.
B. The Union Parliament has exclusive powers over any item not covered in the State or Concurrent Lists.
x: Article 248 gives Parliament exclusive power to legislate on any matter not listed in the State or Concurrent Lists, so both statements are correct.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Match List - I with List - II. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I (Writ) / List - II (Meaning)
a. Quo-Warranto - i. to be certified
b. Mandamus - ii. by what Authority
c. Habeas Corpus - iii. we command
d. Certiorari - iv. to have the body of
x: Quo warranto means 'by what authority', mandamus 'we command', habeas corpus 'to have the body' and certiorari 'to be certified'.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: The concept of Judicial Activism was originated and developed in
x: Judicial activism and judicial review grew out of the US Supreme Court's practice, beginning with Marbury v. Madison (1803).

subject: Indian Constitution
s: The State Election Commission conducts elections to
x: Under Articles 243K and 243ZA the State Election Commission conducts elections to panchayats and municipalities; legislature elections are run by the Election Commission of India.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Arrange the following Committees of Panchayat Raj in chronological order.
a. Gadgil Committee
b. Dantwala Committee
c. L. M. Singhvi Committee
d. Balwant Rai Mehta Committee
x: Balwant Rai Mehta reported in 1957, Dantwala in 1978, L. M. Singhvi in 1986 and the Gadgil Committee in 1988.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 came into force on
x: The 74th Amendment on urban local bodies came into force on 1 June 1993; the 73rd came into force on 24 April 1993.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct ?
A. The Cantonments Act was passed by the Central Legislature in 1924.
B. The first municipal corporation came into existence at Madras in 1688.
C. Lord Rippon is regarded as the Father of Local Self Government in India.
x: The Cantonments Act was passed in 1924, the Madras Municipal Corporation was set up in 1688 and Lord Ripon's 1882 resolution earned him the title Father of Local Self-Government, so all three are correct.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Which of the following statements is/are not true regarding Electronic Voting Machines (EVM) ?
A. EVMs were used for the first time in the entire State of Goa in the general elections to the Assembly in 1999.
B. EVMs were used for the first time on experimental basis in the selected constituencies in the Assembly elections to the States of Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat in 1998.
o: Both A and B are true
x: Goa did use EVMs statewide in its 1999 Assembly election. The 1998 experimental use covered Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Delhi, not Gujarat, so only B is untrue.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: Which of the following Constitution Amendment Acts reduced the minimum age for voting from 21 to 18 years ?
x: The 61st Amendment Act, 1988 amended Article 326 to lower the voting age from 21 to 18.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Match List - I with List - II. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I (Committee) / List - II (Related Electoral Reform)
a. Vohra Committee - i. Amendments to Criminal Law
b. Indrajit Gupta Committee - ii. Electoral Disqualifications
c. Dinesh Goswami Committee - iii. State funding of elections
d. J. S. Varma Committee - iv. Electoral reforms
v. Nexus between crime and politics
x: The Vohra Committee studied the criminal-political nexus, Indrajit Gupta state funding of elections, Dinesh Goswami electoral reforms, and the J. S. Verma Committee amendments to criminal law.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are true relating to Election Commission of India ?
A. The Election Commission of India is a three member Body.
B. The Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of India.
C. Election Commission of India is a Constitutional Body.
x: The ECI is a constitutional body under Article 324 and currently has three members, but the CEC is appointed by the President, not the Chief Justice.

s: main

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
In the list given below, how many are Constitutional Bodies ?
a. NITI Aayog
b. National Commission for Minorities
c. Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
d. National Human Rights Commission
x: Only the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (Article 350B) is constitutional. NITI Aayog is an executive body, and the NCM and NHRC are statutory.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: As per 91st Amendment Act of 2003, the total number of ministers including the Prime Minister, in the Central Council of Ministers shall not exceed ________ of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.
x: Article 75(1A), inserted by the 91st Amendment, caps the Union Council of Ministers at 15 per cent of the Lok Sabha's strength.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: Who described Indian Union as, "a federation with a centralising tendency" ?
x: Sir Ivor Jennings described India as a federation with a strong centralising tendency, while K. C. Wheare called it quasi-federal.

s: intl_org

subject: Indian Constitution
s: The power to increase the number of judges in the Supreme Court of India is vested in
x: Under Article 124(1) Parliament can increase the number of Supreme Court judges by law, through the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Act.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Arrange the following political parties in the chronological order of their establishment.
A. Samaj Wadi Party
B. Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam
C. Bahujan Samaj Party
D. Telugu Desam Party
x: The DMK was founded in 1949, the TDP in 1982, the BSP in 1984 and the Samajwadi Party in 1992.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
As per the provisions of Right to Information Act, the State Chief Information Commissioner is appointed by the Governor, on the recommendations of a committee comprising of,
A. Chief Minister of the concerned State
B. Chief Justice of the concerned State High Court
C. Leader of the Opposition in the State Assembly
D. Cabinet Minister nominated by the Chief Minister
x: Section 15(3) of the RTI Act names the Chief Minister, the Leader of Opposition and a Cabinet Minister nominated by the CM; the High Court Chief Justice is not a member.

s: main

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Which of the following violate the federal principles of the Indian Constitution ?
A. Office of the Governor
B. Central Services
C. Office of the Comptroller and Auditor General
D. Emergency Powers
x: The key treats the Centre-appointed Governor, a single CAG auditing both Union and State accounts, and the emergency powers as departures from federal principles; Central (All India) Services are not counted.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Match List - I with List - II. (Common code for English and Telugu Versions)
List - I (Subject) / List - II (List)
a. Organisation of High Courts - i. Concurrent List
b. Taxes on Mineral Rights - ii. Union List
c. Education - iii. State List
x: Constitution and organisation of High Courts is Union List entry 78, taxes on mineral rights is State List entry 50, and education has been in the Concurrent List since 1976.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: By which of the following Acts, the Governor General of Bengal was designated as the Governor General of India ?
x: The Charter Act of 1833 made the Governor-General of Bengal the Governor-General of India; Lord William Bentinck was the first to hold the title.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: When did The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 come into force ?
x: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act received assent on 1 January 2014 and came into force on 16 January 2014.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
The Parliament can make laws on subjects enumerated in the State list in the following conditions
A. On the request of two or more States.
B. The Rajya Sabha passes a resolution with at least two-thirds of the members present and voting, authorizing the Parliament to make laws on the subject in the national interest.
C. Proclamation of International Agreements.
D. The Lok Sabha passes a resolution with at least two-thirds of the members present and voting, authorizing the Parliament to make laws on the subject in the national interest.
x: Parliament can legislate on State subjects at the request of two or more States (Art. 252), on a Rajya Sabha resolution (Art. 249) and to implement international agreements (Art. 253). A Lok Sabha resolution has no such effect.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: The 11th Fundamental Duty was added by which Constitutional Amendment Act ?
x: The 86th Amendment Act, 2002 added Article 51A(k), the duty of parents to provide education to children aged 6-14.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Assertion (A) : The UPSC is the Central recruiting agency in India.
Reason (R) : It is an independent recruiting constitutional body.
o: Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is not a correct explanation of (A)
x: The UPSC is India's central recruiting agency and is an independent constitutional body under Article 315, but its constitutional status does not explain why it is the recruiting agency.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Assertion (A) : The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act is a significant landmark in the evolution of grassroots democratic institutions in the country.
Reason (R) : This Act has brought the Panchayath Raj institutions under the purview of justiciable part of the Constitution.
o: Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: The 73rd Amendment moved panchayats from the non-justiciable Directive Principles (Article 40) into the justiciable Part IX, giving them constitutional status. That is why it is a landmark.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Assertion (A) : The All India Services violate the federal principle of the Constitution as well as the autonomy of States.
Reason (R) : The All India Service officers are governed by Central Government rules and the State Governments do not have full control over them.
o: Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: All India Service officers serve the States but are recruited and disciplined under central rules, so States lack full control over them. That is the basis of the criticism that these services dilute federalism.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Assertion (A) : NITI Aayog is a Non-Constitutional Advisory Body.
Reason (R) : One of the objectives of NITI Aayog is to develop mechanisms to formulate credible plans at the village level and aggregate these progressively at higher levels of government.
o: Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are True but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: NITI Aayog was created by an executive resolution in 2015, and bottom-up village-level planning is one of its stated objectives. That objective does not explain why it is non-constitutional.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Assertion (A) : Article 263 contemplates the establishment of an Inter-State Council to effect co-ordination between the States and between Center and the States.
Reason (R) : Rajmannar Committee made a strong case for establishment of the Inter-State Council.
o: Both (A) and (R) are True and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are True but (R) is not a correct explanation of (A)
x: Article 263 provides for an Inter-State Council, and the Rajamannar Committee (1969) did urge setting one up. The committee's recommendation came long after the Article and does not explain it.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Which of the following will be the correct consequences of declaration of National Emergency by the President ?
A. The President can modify the constitutional distribution of finances between the Center and the States.
B. The Center becomes entitled to give executive directions to a State on any matter.
C. The President can suspend all the Fundamental Rights of the citizens.
x: During a national emergency the President can modify revenue sharing (Art. 354) and the Centre can direct States on any matter (Art. 353). Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended, so C is wrong.

s: extreme

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Which of the following statements are correct ?
A. Public Interest Litigation (PIL) is also known as Social Action Litigation.
B. PIL is an outcome of Judicial Restraint.
C. Justice V. R. Krishna Iyer and Justice P. N. Bhagawathi were pioneers of the concept of PIL.
x: PIL is also called social action litigation and was pioneered by Justices Krishna Iyer and Bhagwati. It grew out of judicial activism, not judicial restraint, so B is wrong.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: Which of the following is not on Center - State Relations ?
x: The Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) dealt with state funding of elections. Sarkaria, Rajamannar and Punchhi all examined Centre-State relations.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: Which of the following is not a condition for the political party to be recognised as National Party ?
o: The party wins two percent of seats in the Lok Sabha from at least three different states

The party, at a general election to Lok Sabha or Legislative Assembly, polls six percent of valid votes in any four or more States and in addition it wins four Lok Sabha seats from any State or States
It is recognised as a State party in any four States
x: Each of the three listed conditions is one of the alternative criteria under the Election Symbols Order for national party status, so 'None of the above' is correct.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Which of the following statements is/are not correct regarding the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act ?
A. 18 functional items were placed within the purview of Panchayats.
B. The Act does not apply to the States of Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram.
C. The Act bars interference by courts in the electoral matters of Panchayats.
D. Reservation of seats to BCs is a compulsory provision under this Act.
x: The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 subjects, not 18, and reservation for backward classes is left to the States. B and C are correct provisions (Articles 243M and 243O).

s: binding

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
The President is elected by an Electoral College consisting of
A. Elected members of both Houses of Parliament.
B. Nominated members of both Houses of Parliament.
C. The elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of all the States.
D. Nominated members of the Legislative Assemblies of all the States.
E. The elected members of the Legislative Assemblies of NCT of Delhi and the Union Territory of Puducherry.
o: A, B, C, D and E
x: Under Article 54 the electoral college has only elected members of Parliament, the State Assemblies and the Assemblies of Delhi and Puducherry; nominated members do not vote.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts was declared unconstitutional and void by the Supreme Court in 2015 ?
x: In the Fourth Judges case (October 2015) the Supreme Court struck down the 99th Amendment, which had created the National Judicial Appointments Commission.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Match List - I with List - II and choose the right answer from the codes given below. (Common code for English and Telugu Versions) :
List - I / List - II
a. Separate representation of the Muslim Community - i. Government of India Act, 1935
b. Dyarchy in the provinces - ii. Indian Councils Act, 1892
c. Prescribed Federation - iii. Indian Councils Act, 1909
d. Discussion of Annual Statement - iv. Indian Councils Act, 1861
v. Government of India Act, 1919
x: Separate electorates for Muslims came with the 1909 Act, provincial dyarchy with the 1919 Act and the proposed All-India Federation with the 1935 Act. The 1892 Act allowed discussion of the annual financial statement.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding Finance Commission ?
o: Finance Commission is a Quasi-judicial Body
Finance Commission consists of a Chairman and four other members
Article 290 provides for the Constitution of Finance Commission
x: The Finance Commission is set up under Article 280. Article 290 deals with adjustment of certain expenses and pensions.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: Which of the following objectives is not embodied in the Preamble to the Constitution of India ?
x: The Preamble promises liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship, and political justice. 'Political liberty' is not among its words.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Which of the following statements about the Attorney General of India is/are correct ?
i. The President shall appoint a person who is qualified to be appointed a Judge of the Supreme Court to be Attorney General of India.
ii. He shall have right of audience in all courts in the territory of India.
iii. He shall hold office during the pleasure of the Prime Minister.
iv. He shall receive remuneration as the Parliament may determine.
x: Under Article 76 the AG must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge and has right of audience in all courts. He holds office at the pleasure of the President, not the PM, and his remuneration is fixed by the President, not Parliament.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Match the Constitutions of different countries given in List - A with their Provisions given in List - B which are adopted in Indian Constitution. (Common code for English and Telugu Versions)
List - A / List - B
a. UK Constitution - i. The idea of Residual Powers
b. Irish Constitution - ii. The idea of Rule of Law
c. United States of America Constitution - iii. Directive Principles of State Policy
d. Canadian Constitution - iv. Power of Judicial Review
x: India took the rule of law from the UK, the Directive Principles from Ireland, judicial review from the USA and the vesting of residuary powers in the Centre from Canada.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Which of the following statements are correct about Presidential system ?
i. President is head of the State.
ii. President is head of the Government.
iii. President is directly elected by the people.
iv. President is accountable to legislature.
o: Only i, ii and iv are correct
Only i and iii are correct
Only i, ii and iii are correct
Only ii and iv are correct
x: In a presidential system the President is both head of state and head of government and is elected by the people for a fixed term. He is not accountable to the legislature.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Which of the following statements about State Finance Commission is/are correct ?
i. This Commission examines the financial position of the local governments in the State.
ii. It also reviews the distribution of revenues between the State and Local governments on the one hand and between rural and urban local governments on the other.
x: Under Articles 243-I and 243Y the State Finance Commission reviews the finances of panchayats and municipalities and recommends how revenues should be shared, so both statements are correct.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Which of the following statements about the Vice President of India are correct ?
i. The Vice President is elected for five years.
ii. The Vice President acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.
iii. The Vice President acts as the President only until a new President is elected.
x: The Vice President has a five-year term, is ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and, in a vacancy, acts as President only until a new President is elected.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: In which of the following hours, members of the Parliament are free to raise any matter that they think is important ?
x: Zero Hour is an informal Indian practice in which members raise urgent matters without prior notice; Question Hour is limited to questions admitted in advance.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: The most powerful weapon that enables the Parliament to ensure executive accountability is
x: A no-confidence motion can remove the Council of Ministers, which is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha under Article 75(3), so it is the strongest accountability tool.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Correctly match the following in List - A with List - B. (Common codes for English and Telugu Versions)
List - A / List - B
a. Art. 137 - i. Restoring Fundamental Rights by Supreme Court by issuing writs.
b. Art. 226 - ii. Power of Supreme Court to review any judgment pronounced or Order made by it.
c. Art. 13 - iii. The High Courts also have the power to issue Writs for protecting Fundamental Rights.
d. Art. 32 - iv. Supreme Court can declare the concerned law as unconstitutional.
x: Article 137 lets the Supreme Court review its own judgments, Article 226 gives High Courts writ powers, Article 13 voids laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights, and Article 32 lets the Supreme Court enforce them by writs.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: The Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act came into effect on
x: The J&K Reorganisation Act, 2019 took effect on 31 October 2019, creating the Union Territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Assertion (A) : Right to Property is made a legal right under Article 300-A in Part XII of the Constitution.
Reason (R) : 44th Amendment Act of 1978 eliminated the Right to Property from the list of Fundamental Rights.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: The 44th Amendment deleted Articles 19(1)(f) and 31 from the Fundamental Rights and, in their place, made property a constitutional (legal) right under Article 300A.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: Regarding the Panchayat Raj System, in 1978 Ashok Mehta Committee recommended for
o: two tier system with four years of term
three tier system with four years of term
two tier system with five years of term
three tier system with six years of term
x: The Ashok Mehta Committee recommended a two-tier system of Zilla Parishad and Mandal Panchayat with a four-year term.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Of the following, which are the appointments made by the President on the recommendation of the Prime Minister ?
i. Chief Justice of India
ii. Judges of Supreme Court and High Courts
iii. Attorney General of India
iv. Governors of States
x: The key treats all four as formal appointments made by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers under Article 74.

s: main

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Which of the following provisions of 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act related to Panchayat Raj Institutions is/are correct ?
i. The members of these bodies are directly elected by the people.
ii. Elections shall be held within a period of 3 months from the dissolution of the body.
iii. Women have been given 1/3rd reservation in Panchayats.
iv. The minimum age required to become member is 21 years.
x: Article 243E requires fresh elections within six months of dissolution, not three, so ii is wrong. Direct election, one-third reservation for women and the minimum age of 21 are correct.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Consider the following statements :
Assertion (A) : One of the most controversial Articles in the Constitution is Article 356.
Reason (R) : It is imposed when the Government of the State cannot be carried on in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: Article 356 (President's Rule) applies when a State's government cannot be carried on according to the Constitution. That broad, subjective ground is why it has been so often misused and so controversial.

constitution

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Assertion (A) : Mandamus normally is not issued to Govt. for making law.
Reason (R) : Mandamus cannot lie in absence of policy. Once policy is laid down, terms of policy can be enforced.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: Courts do not issue mandamus directing the government to legislate or frame policy; mandamus can only enforce a duty under an existing law or policy. That is why (R) explains (A).

s: extreme

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Assertion (A) : Directive Principles of State Policy are not capable of being independently enforced in a Court of Law.
Reason (R) : They act as guide post for legislation.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
x: Article 37 makes the Directive Principles non-justiciable yet fundamental in governance, and they guide legislation. In its final key APPSC changed the answer from (1) to (2): both statements are true, but serving as a guide for legislation is not why they are unenforceable.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Are the statements given below in the Indian Constitution ?
Statement (A) : Ownership and control of the material resources of the community are so distributed as best to subserve the common good.
Statement (B) : Operation of the economic system does not result in the concentration of wealth and means of production to the common detriment.
o: Both Statements (A) and (B) are not there
x: Both statements are in the Constitution, as Article 39(b) and Article 39(c) of the Directive Principles.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Directive Principles of State Policy contain which of the following ?
a. Free Legal Aid
b. Maternity Relief
c. Living Wage
d. Safeguarding of Forests
e. Protection of Monuments
o: a, b, c, d and e
x: Free legal aid (39A), maternity relief (42), living wage (43), protecting forests (48A) and protecting monuments (49) are all Directive Principles.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: Panchayats have responsibilities in respect of which of the following as per the Eleventh Schedule ?
x: Libraries are item 20 of the Eleventh Schedule. Slaughter houses, regulation of land use and burial grounds are Twelfth Schedule (municipal) items.

subject: Indian Constitution
s: Municipalities have Constitutional responsibilities in respect of which of the following as per the Twelfth Schedule ?
x: Cattle pounds and prevention of cruelty to animals are in the Twelfth Schedule. The other three options are Eleventh Schedule (panchayat) items.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Statement (A) : There is no fundamental right to marry.
Statement (B) : Right to travel abroad comes under the purview of Fundamental Rights.
o: Statement (A) is right and Statement (B) is wrong
Statement (A) is wrong and Statement (B) is right
x: APPSC's key accepts (A), since there is no separately listed fundamental right to marry. Since Maneka Gandhi (1978), the right to travel abroad is part of personal liberty under Article 21, so (B) is right too.

s: extreme

subject: Indian Constitution
s: Which of the following is not a Fundamental Duty as mentioned in the Constitution ?
o: To safeguard public property and to abjure violence
To value and preserve the rich heritage of the country's composite culture
To protect the elderly, differently abled and children
To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood
x: Article 51A has no duty to protect the elderly and differently abled; the other three are listed duties.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct ?
i. Under Section 81 of the Representation of the People Act (RPA) 1951, no election can be called in question except by an election petition presented in accordance with the provisions of this part.
ii. Only the High Courts have original jurisdiction on deciding on election petitions.
iii. An election petition calling in question an election shall be filed within the time period of 30 days from the date of declaration of results.
x: The bar on challenging elections except by petition is in Section 80 of the RPA, not Section 81, and petitions must be filed within 45 days, not 30. Election petitions are tried by the High Court, so only ii is correct.

s: extreme
only

subject: Indian Constitution

With reference to the Indian Judiciary, which of the following statement(s) is/are correct ?
i. Any retired judge of the Supreme Court of India can be called back to sit and act as a Supreme Court Judge by the Chief Justice of India with the prior permission of the President of India.
ii. A High Court in India has the power to review its own Judgement as the Supreme Court does although there has been no specific power of review conferred on it by the Constitution.
x: Article 128 lets the CJI, with the President's prior consent, ask a retired Supreme Court judge to sit again. As courts of record, High Courts also have an inherent power to review their own judgments. In its final key APPSC changed the answer from (1) to (3).

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Assertion (A) : The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act (1976) is known as 'Mini-Constitution'.
Reason (R) : The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act (1976) made changes to the Preamble, the Seventh Schedule and to 54 Articles of the Constitution.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation for (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation for (A)
x: The 42nd Amendment is widely called the 'mini-Constitution' because of how much it changed. APPSC's key treats (R) as false because its description of the extent of the changes (54 Articles) is not accurate.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Which of the following statements regarding the administration of tribal areas under the Sixth Schedule of the Constitution is/are correct ?
i. It is applicable in all States where Scheduled Tribes make up more than 40% of the State's population.
ii. These areas are outside the authority of the State Legislature as well as State Executive.
iii. Only the President can organise and reorganise the autonomous districts in these areas.
iv. The High Court of the State does not have any jurisdiction in these areas.
x: The Sixth Schedule applies only to tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. The Governor, not the President, organises autonomous districts, and the State's executive and High Court still have jurisdiction. All four statements are wrong.

subject: Indian Constitution
s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct ?
i. Floating Constituencies are the constituencies without fixed geographical borders.
ii. In the constituency of Sangha in Sikkim, only Buddhist monks can contest and vote.
x: Sikkim's Sangha seat is a non-territorial ('floating') constituency with no fixed boundaries, in which only registered lamas and monks of the Buddhist monasteries can stand and vote. Both statements are correct.
